bots.name: AI2Bot
bots.description: The Allen Institute for AI's crawler, used to build open training datasets such as Dolma. It crawls selected domains for web content that is then used to train open language models. Ai2 runs it under two user agents, a plain AI2Bot and an Ai2Bot-Dolma variant that names the dataset, both pointing at the same crawling notice. Ai2 publishes no IP ranges, ASN, or reverse-DNS pattern, and its crawling notice offers user-agent filtering as the only documented control.

bots.name: Amazon Bedrock Web Crawler
bots.description: The web crawler AWS runs for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, which fetches the site URLs an AWS customer has configured as a data source and ingests the pages into that customer's knowledge base. Like Google-CloudVertexBot it is customer-directed but operator-run: the requests come from Amazon's infrastructure, and AWS requires the customer to confirm they are authorised to crawl the domains they supply. AWS documents that the crawler follows robots.txt per RFC 9309 and that it defaults to disallow when a site serves no robots.txt at all.

bots.name: Amazonbot
bots.description: Amazon's web crawler used to improve Amazon's products and services, including training AI models. Amazon publishes the crawler's source addresses on its own bot page as a dated snapshot; they are recorded here verbatim.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko; compatible; Amazonbot/0.1) Chrome/W.X.Y.Z Safari/537.36

bots.name: Bytespider
bots.description: ByteDance's web crawler, used to gather training data for its AI models. ByteDance publishes no IP ranges, ASN, or reverse-DNS pattern for it.

bots.name: CCBot
bots.description: Common Crawl's crawler that builds the freely available Common Crawl web archive, widely reused as AI training data by third parties.

bots.name: Claude-SearchBot
bots.description: Anthropic's crawler that indexes pages to improve search-style answer quality in Claude products, distinct from ClaudeBot's training-data crawl.

bots.name: ClaudeBot
bots.description: Anthropic's web crawler collecting publicly available web data for training Claude models. Anthropic publishes its crawler source IPs as a machine-readable feed.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko; compatible; ClaudeBot/1.0; +claudebot@anthropic.com)

bots.name: Cloudflare AI Search
bots.description: The crawler behind Cloudflare AI Search, which indexes website content so it can be searched. Cloudflare documents that it only crawls a website the customer owns — the domain must exist in the same Cloudflare account and be selected as an AI Search data source.

bots.name: Cloudflare Browser Run Crawler
bots.description: The crawler behind the /crawl endpoint of Cloudflare's Browser Run (Browser Rendering) developer product, which crawls third-party websites on behalf of Cloudflare customers building applications on the platform. Its user agent is not configurable, and every request is signed with Web Bot Auth HTTP message signatures that site owners can verify against Cloudflare's published key directory.

bots.name: Diffbot
bots.description: Diffbot's general-purpose web crawler, used to build its Knowledge Graph and power its structured-extraction APIs. Diffbot documents robots.txt behavior but publishes no IP list, ASN, or reverse-DNS pattern.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.1; en-US; rv:1.9.1.2) Gecko/20090729 Firefox/3.5.2 (.NET CLR 3.5.30729; Diffbot/0.1; +http://www.diffbot.com)

bots.name: FirecrawlAgent
bots.description: The fetcher behind Firecrawl's scraping and crawling API, which retrieves web pages on behalf of the developers and AI agents calling that API. Firecrawl's crawl endpoint honours robots.txt by default; ignoring it is an enterprise option that must be enabled by the operator. Firecrawl documents that it does not use a fixed set of outbound IP addresses.

bots.name: Gist Crawler Bot
bots.description: ProRata.ai's crawler for Gist.ai. It systematically fetches licensed and publicly accessible content to power the retrieval-augmented generation model behind Gist Answers, following internal and external links to discover new and changed pages, and may also download the CSS and JavaScript a page needs for accurate content extraction. ProRata documents that the crawler only visits content that is either freely accessible without credentials or explicitly licensed, spaces out its requests, and publishes the two addresses it crawls from, one for production and one for testing.

bots.name: Google-CloudVertexBot
bots.description: Google Cloud crawler that fetches sites on the site owners' request when building Vertex AI Agents. Crawling preferences addressed to its user agent have no effect on Google Search or other Google products.

bots.name: GPTBot
bots.description: OpenAI's web crawler that gathers publicly available data used to train OpenAI's models.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; GPTBot/1.2; +https://openai.com/gptbot

bots.name: ICC-Crawler

operator.name: National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT)

bots.description: The web crawler of the Universal Communication Research Institute at Japan's National Institute of Information and Communications Technology. It collects web pages for NICT's research and development of information processing technologies including multilingual translation, information analysis and artificial intelligence, and NICT states that collected information and research products may be provided to third parties for joint or further research. The crawler page documents a load policy that caps connections per unit of time across a host's several addresses or hostnames.

bots.name: ImagesiftBot
bots.description: ImageSift's crawler, operated by Hive. It scrapes publicly available images across the web to support Hive's ImageSift reverse-image-search and web intelligence products. Standard robots.txt directives are respected.

bots.name: Kimi-SearchBot
bots.description: Moonshot AI's search crawler for Kimi, which analyses pages for relevance and builds the index behind Kimi's search features. Blocking it removes a site from Kimi search results. Listed separately from KimiBot because Moonshot documents it as an independently configurable crawler with its own robots.txt token and its own published address list.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; Kimi-SearchBot/1.0; +https://www.kimi.com/policies/kimi-crawlers

bots.name: KimiBot
bots.description: Moonshot AI's crawler for the Kimi assistant, gathering content that may be used to train Kimi's foundation models. Moonshot documents robots.txt control per crawler and publishes a machine-readable list of the addresses its crawlers use, while noting the ranges are dynamic and may change.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; KimiBot/1.0; +https://www.kimi.com/policies/kimi-crawlers

bots.name: KlaviyoAIBot
bots.description: The crawler behind Klaviyo's Kai Customer Agent. It fetches publicly available pages only from the domains and URLs a Klaviyo customer has explicitly connected to their own account — their store plus any help centre, documentation portal, blog or news source they add — and indexes them so Klaviyo can answer shopper questions and generate content. Klaviyo documents that it does not bypass authentication, paywalls or access controls, that it slows down on 429 and 503 responses with Retry-After, and that it deletes indexed content within days once a page is removed or disallowed.

bots.name: Leipzig Corpora Collection Crawler

operator.name: Leipzig University Natural Language Processing Group

bots.description: The LCC crawler is operated by Leipzig University to collect web text for the Leipzig Corpora Collection, a set of linguistic corpora used in natural language processing research.

bots.name: LinerBot
bots.description: Web crawler operated by Liner, an AI search and research assistant, which gathers pages from the public web and indexes them so Liner's search and research agents can retrieve and cite them. Liner's crawler page documents the user agent, states that access is controlled through robots.txt, and gives worked examples for both a full disallow and path-scoped allow rules.

instances: Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko; compatible; LinerBot/1.0; +https://docs.getliner.com/docs/linerbot)

bots.name: LinkupBot
bots.description: Linkup's web crawler. It discovers and retrieves publicly accessible pages to build and maintain the Linkup search index, which powers search and web grounding for AI applications. Linkup publishes the CIDR ranges its crawler originates from and asks site owners to check both the source IP and the user-agent token, since user agents can be spoofed.

instances: LinkupBot/1.0 (LinkupBot for web indexing; https://www.linkup.so/bot; bot@linkup.so)

bots.name: MaCoCu
bots.description: Crawler for the CEF-funded MaCoCu project, which collects, curates and enriches monolingual and parallel web text to build language corpora for under-resourced languages. The project publishes no IP ranges, so requests cannot be verified.

bots.name: Meta External Agent
bots.description: Meta's crawler for AI training data and content indexing across Meta products. Verified by ASN lookup (AS32934); Meta publishes no IP feed.

bots.name: Meta Web Indexer
bots.description: Meta's crawler that navigates the web to improve the quality of Meta AI search results, analysing page content for relevance and accuracy in Meta AI responses. Verified by ASN lookup (AS32934); Meta publishes no IP feed.

bots.name: MistralAI-Index
bots.description: Mistral AI's indexing crawler. It crawls the web automatically to build the index behind Mistral search, which answers user questions in Vibe. Mistral documents that content collected by this crawler is not used for generative AI training of any kind, and publishes the crawler's addresses as a JSON feed.

bots.name: MistralAI-Training

It collects web content to help build the datasets used to train Mistral's generative AI models, and is documented as separate from both the search-index crawler and the user-triggered fetcher. Mistral states webmasters can disallow this user agent in robots.txt.

bots.description: ICC-Crawler is a web crawler operated by Japan's NICT that collects web pages across the internet to build datasets for information and language processing research.

bots.name: NoahBot
bots.description: The crawler powering Noah Wire's search and research engine for journalists and editors. It scans publicly accessible news sources — press releases, newsrooms, blogs and announcement feeds — and the operator states it does not scrape, store or republish full articles, producing linked summaries instead. The bot page says requests are signed with HTTP Message Signatures, but publishes no key directory URL, so no verification recipe is recorded.
